result.title: CivicBench: A Benchmark and Memory Framework for Web-Based Civic Data Analytics
result.summary: Municipalities publish service requests, geographic boundaries, weather observations, demographic estimates, and operational guidance through independently maintained Web portals. Civic analysis must combine these sources while preserving their schemas, source links, spatial and temporal scopes, and interpretive limits. Tool-using language agents can perform this integration, but existing task benchmarks rarely test whether a computed claim remains supported by the records used. We present CivicBench, a 400-task benchmark over four cities and two years that materializes civic Web data into frozen bundles for reproducible evaluation. Executable contracts score computation, source linkage, coverage, scope, qualified answers, and refusal when the requested conclusion is not supported. We also introduce Task-State Memory (TSM), which compiles tool observations into typed assertions, reconciles records only within compatible scopes, and retrieves a bounded state organized around unresolved constraints. Across nine completed model pairs, eight yield positive mean-score differences with 95\% semantic-contract-cluster bootstrap intervals excluding zero; the ninth interval crosses zero. The benchmark and memory framework make the records behind a claim inspectable at the point of decision.

AI.brief_summary: CivicBench 提出覆盖四城市两年的 400 项市政 Web 数据分析任务基准，用可执行契约评分计算、来源链接、覆盖范围与证据不足时的拒答，并提出把工具观测编译为带类型断言、仅在兼容范围内对齐的有界状态记忆 TSM。
AI.relevance_reason: 其带类型断言、范围对齐的有界状态与基于记录支撑度的拒答评分，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、推理状态组织与 STOP 决策的表示及评价设计，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理。
